extra.message: The 'copyline' query parameter of GET /ops/copy/ticket-copy-badge-028 is concatenated directly into an HTML string that is returned via HTMLResponse without any escaping or sanitization. An attacker can inject arbitrary JavaScript, e.g. ?copyline=, yielding reflected cross-site scripting in any browser context that renders the response.

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

extra.message: POST /ops/workset/ticket-workset-rebind-029 merges the entire user-supplied JSON body into the server-side 'workset' object via workset.update(change_set). The request body can override security-relevant attributes that were intentionally defaulted to safe values, including 'is_admin': False, 'role': 'viewer', and 'credit_limit', allowing an attacker to escalate the object to is_admin=True.

cwe: CWE-915: Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes
CWE-284: Improper Access Control

extra.message: GET /ops/brief/ticket-agent-packet-030 returns a hardcoded live partner token ('tok_live_partner_sync') and an SSN-format tax reference ('739-44-1982') in the response body. Any caller able to reach the endpoint obtains these sensitive credentials and personally identifiable information.

cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor
CWE-798: Use of Hard-coded Credentials

extra.message: GET /ops/after/ticket-lane-148 redirects to the user-controlled 'lane' query parameter via RedirectResponse(lane) without validating that it is a safe relative path or trusted host. An attacker can craft /ops/after/ticket-lane-148?lane=https://evil.example to redirect victims to a malicious site (open redirect, usable for phishing).

cwe: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site ('Open Redirect')

extra.message: POST /ops/wire/ticket-tally-210 logs the raw request body together with the client's Authorization header at WARNING level (logger.warning(... request.headers.get("authorization"))). Bearer tokens/API credentials submitted by callers are written verbatim into application logs where they may be read by anyone with log access.

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

extra.message: POST /ops/vault/ticket-stash-232 builds a file path from the user-controlled 'ref' query/body value (BASE_EXPORT_DIR / f"{ref}.json") without any traversal check, then writes JSON content to it with target.write_text(...). A ref such as '../../etc/cron.d/pwn' escapes the export directory and writes an attacker-influenced JSON file (which also embeds SSN/card values) to an arbitrary location on the filesystem.

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

extra.message: POST /ops/digest/ticket-fold-272 computes a digest of user-supplied input with hashlib.md5(). MD5 is a cryptographically broken hash function (collision-prone, unsuitable for any security purpose); a modern algorithm such as SHA-256 must be used instead.

cwe: CWE-327: Use of a Broken or Risky Cryptographic Algorithm

extra.message: GET /ops/spool/ticket-fan-307 accepts an unbounded 'count' query parameter and materializes a list of 'count' dicts in memory ([{"idx": idx, "ref": ref} for idx in range(count)]) with no upper limit. A request such as ?count=999999999 causes memory/CPU exhaustion, a denial of service against the process.

cwe: CWE-400: Uncontrolled Resource Consumption
CWE-770: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling

extra.message: GET /ops/relay/ticket-probe-354 passes the fully user-controlled 'endpoint' query parameter directly to urllib.request.urlopen(). The server can be made to issue requests to arbitrary targets, including internal-only services (e.g. http://169.254.169.254/ cloud metadata, internal admin panels) and file:// URLs for local file reads, with the first 2KB of the response returned to the caller — a full server-side request forgery primitive.

cwe: CWE-918: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)

extra.message: GET /ops/origin/ticket-mirror-368 reflects the caller's Origin header verbatim into the Access-Control-Allow-Origin response header and additionally sets Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true. This allows any malicious origin to make credentialed cross-origin requests to the application and read the responses, completely defeating the same-origin policy for this endpoint.

cwe: CWE-942: Permissive Cross-domain Policy with Untrusted Domains
CWE-16: Configuration

extra.message: GET /ops/jinja/ticket-cast-378 compiles the user-controlled 'fragment' query parameter as a Jinja2 template (Template("Result: " + fragment).render()) and returns the rendered result as HTML. This is a textbook server-side template injection leading to remote code execution, e.g. ?fragment={{ ''.__class__.__mro__[1].__subclasses__() }}.

cwe: CWE-1336: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements Used in a Template Engine
CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')

extra.message: POST /ops/dock/ticket-shelf-387 joins the user-controlled 'name' query parameter to the base export directory (BASE_EXPORT_DIR / name) with no sanitization or containment check and writes the raw request body to the resulting path via target.write_bytes(body). A name such as '../../app/seed.py' or an absolute path permits arbitrary file overwrite/write anywhere the process can write, leading to code execution by overwriting application files.

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

extra.message: GET /ops/shell/ticket-probe-398 builds a shell command by concatenating the user-controlled 'host' query parameter and executes it via os.system("ping -c 1 " + host). Because os.system() invokes a shell, input such as ?host=127.0.0.1;whoami or ?host=$(id) results in arbitrary OS command execution on the server.

cwe: CWE-78: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')

extra.message: GET /ops/nonce/ticket-roll-408 generates a security token ('code') with the non-cryptographic random module (random.choice(...)). The Python 'random' PRNG is predictable (state can be recovered from observed outputs), so any nonce/one-time code produced by this endpoint is guessable; the 'secrets' module must be used instead.

cwe: CWE-338: Use of Cryptographically Weak Pseudo-Random Number Generator (PRNG)

extra.message: POST /ops/mongo/ticket-lane-418 passes the user-supplied JSON payload (payload.get("filter", payload)) directly as the MongoDB query filter to find_one(query). An attacker can inject MongoDB query operators — e.g. {"filter": {"$where": "sleep(10000)"}} or {"username": {"$ne": ""}} — to manipulate or bypass the intended query and read arbitrary documents, whose repr is returned in the response.

cwe: CWE-943: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Data Query Logic

extra.message: GET /ops/trust/ticket-drift-428 creates an SSL context with certificate verification disabled (ssl._create_unverified_context()) and uses it for the outbound HTTPS request to the partner endpoint. Disabling peer certificate validation exposes the connection to man-in-the-middle attacks; the endpoint even advertises 'verify_peer': False in its response.

cwe: CWE-295: Improper Certificate Validation

extra.message: GET /ops/badge/ticket-gate-438 makes an authorization decision solely on a value the client fully controls: badge = request.cookies.get("ops_badge") or request.headers.get("x-ops-badge", ""), and if badge == "lead" it returns the elevated lane with payroll/casework data. Any caller can trivially set the ops_badge cookie or x-ops-badge header to "lead" and gain the privileged result — an authentication/authorization bypass.

cwe: CWE-807: Reliance on Untrusted Inputs in a Security Decision
CWE-863: Incorrect Authorization

extra.message: GET /ops/trace/ticket-panel-448 discloses internal deployment details to any caller: the value of the APP_ENV environment variable and the absolute path of the private export directory on the server. This information aids attackers in fingerprinting the environment and targeting the path-traversal write endpoints in this same module.

cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

extra.message: The application's session-token signing key is hardcoded as a default value (secret_key = "dev-only-change-me-in-prod-fb7c8c8a5d4f4e9b8a1c2d3e4f5a6b7c") and is used to sign all HS256 JWTs in security.py. Nothing enforces overriding it, so any deployment that boots with defaults lets an attacker who knows this public repo value forge valid session tokens for arbitrary users (complete authentication bypass).

cwe: CWE-798: Use of Hard-coded Credentials

extra.message: The session cookie is configured with secure=False by default (cookie_secure: bool = False), so the HttpOnly session cookie carrying the JWT is transmitted over unencrypted HTTP. If the application is served behind HTTPS without flipping this flag, the session token can be intercepted by a network attacker.

cwe: CWE-614: Sensitive Cookie in HTTPS Session Without 'Secure' Attribute
CWE-16: Configuration

extra.message: POST /api/auth/register returns HTTP 409 when the submitted email already exists (raise HTTPException(status.HTTP_409_CONFLICT, ...)) but 201 on success, despite the inline comment claiming to 'behave the same as success'. The differing status code is an observable response discrepancy that lets an attacker enumerate which email addresses are registered, defeating the anti-enumeration intent stated in the code.

cwe: CWE-203: Observable Discrepancy
CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor
